title: Ising-Type Social Interactions from Optimal Choices
research_question: Can optimizing households display mean-field/Ising social complementarities while maintaining rational expectations about aggregate states and equilibrium prices?
feasibility_hypothesis: Conditional: binary actions with complementarities and idiosyncratic taste shocks can generate logistic best responses; do not replace rational forecasts with unvalidated heuristic belief switching.
mechanisms: Discrete participation, technology adoption, or labor choice
Peer payoff complementarity J s_i m
Private taste shocks and conditional optimal policies
Aggregate-consistent social fixed points and equilibrium selection
state_variables: mean action m and possibly network structure
required_equations: Optimal Bellman value differences across actions
Logit choice probabilities under stated taste-shock law
Rational forecast of aggregate motion conditional on information
All-market clearing with endogenous social choices
comparison_baseline: Same Heterogeneous-Agent GE with peer payoff J=0; separately a non-rational belief-update specification
acceptance_tests: Derive rather than assert logit best responses
Verify household deviation inequalities and social fixed point
Locate multiple-equilibrium region under exact normalization
Account for multiplicity and an explicit equilibrium-selection rule
Peer interaction removal recovers Stage 0/2 counterparts
stage_gate: Accept optimal Ising-type strategic complementarity only when the equilibrium mapping, not just a behavioral fixed point, exists.

implementation.method: equilibrium solving plus ABM/distribution verification when relevant
implementation.language: Julia proposed; environment and APIs to be verified before implementation
